You are a careful, neutral coder of the STRUCTURE OF A CORPORATE TRANSACTION AT
CLOSING. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from public primary sources
(SEC filings, company releases, reputable press). This slice describes ONLY how the
deal was structured -- what crossed the ownership boundary and what did not -- at
the moment of closing. You are DELIBERATELY NOT shown what happened to the combined
company afterward, and you must NOT speculate about later outcomes, success, or
failure. Code STRICTLY the deal as structured. If the slice does not let you
determine a field, you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from
outside knowledge of the companies.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

A. BUNDLE SIGNATURE -- for each of six organizational tiers, classify what happened
to that tier when the transaction crossed the ownership boundary. Exactly one label
per tier.
  T1 Owner Intent (controlling principal / imprint).
     Labels: replace, imprint-share, continue, terminate, reconstruct, replicate, mutual-replace, uncertain.
       replace = old controlling intent exited, a new one installed;
       imprint-share = both principals' intent co-present;
       continue = same controlling intent persists;
       terminate = the controlling intent ended with no successor;
       reconstruct = intent re-formed into a new (often non-commercial) purpose;
       replicate = intent copied into a standardized template (e.g. franchising);
       mutual-replace = two intents fused into a jointly-new one (merger of equals).
  T2 Business Model, T3 Business Entity (legal vehicle), T4 Product (customer-
  acceptance layer), T5 Process (operations), T6 Organization (people/culture).
     Labels for T2-T6: 1-1, N-1, 1-N, subset, partial, read-only, swap, terminate, null, uncertain.
       1-1 = transferred whole, one-to-one; N-1 = many collapsed into one;
       1-N = one split into many; subset = only part transferred;
       partial = transferred but incompletely / with friction;
       read-only = licensed / accessed without ownership transfer;
       swap = exchanged for a different one (e.g. new legal domicile);
       terminate = ended; null = not applicable / nothing at this tier.

B. TIER-TRANSFER GAPS -- code strictly from the STRUCTURE OF THE DEAL AT CLOSING.
A gap is a STRUCTURAL MISMATCH IN WHAT THE DEAL TRANSFERRED, not a later failure.
  gap_45: Did the customer-facing product/asset (T4, what customers buy) cross the
    ownership boundary WITHOUT the operational processes that produce or deliver it
    (T5) transferring or being aligned coherently alongside it? A documented
    product-vs-process structural mismatch AT CLOSING. 1 = yes such a gap; 0 = no
    (product and its processes moved together, or neither moved); uncertain.
  gap_56: Did the operational processes (T5) transfer or get re-engineered WITHOUT
    the organization / people / management / culture that run them (T6) transferring
    or aligning coherently alongside, AT CLOSING? 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  gap_mitigated: If (and only if) you coded a structural gap above, was that gap
    documented as contractually absorbed at closing via a transitional-services or
    operating agreement allocating the shared substrate? yes / no / NA (NA if no gap).

E. collapse_state: Any Tier-1 fusion documented in the deal structure? none /
   T1=T4 (founder identity IS the product) / T1=T3 (the legal subject IS a specific
   natural person) / T1=T3=T4 / T1=T2 / T1=T6 / uncertain.

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your gap_45 and gap_56
codes specifically. Cite ONLY closing-structure evidence; do NOT reason about later
outcomes.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: inability to determine a

[SLICE BEGIN]
# Structural sub-dossier — The Hertz Corporation acquisition of Advantage Rent A Car assets (closing structure, April 2009)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier describes ONLY how the
> transaction was structured at closing — what crossed the ownership boundary and what
> did not. It contains no post-transaction outcome information.

## Note on the drawn filing
- The drawn Form 8-K (filed 2009-08-03; earliest event 2009-07-29) is a Regulation FD /
  Item 2.02 disclosure: it furnishes, as Exhibit 99.1, the slides that accompanied Hertz
  Global Holdings' July 29, 2009 earnings conference call for the quarter ended June 30,
  2009. It is not a transaction-terms document and does not describe an acquisition's
  structure. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-09-046576, Form 8-K Item 2.02]
- The registrant is The Hertz Corporation (Delaware; Commission File No. 001-07541), an
  indirect subsidiary of Hertz Global Holdings, Inc. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-09-046576, Form 8-K]
- The closing-era transaction described below is sourced from the registrant's
  contemporaneous annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2009.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]

## Transaction and parties at closing
- In April 2009 the registrant completed the acquisition of certain assets of Advantage
  Rent A Car ("Advantage"), described as a brand focused on price-oriented customers at
  key U.S. leisure travel destinations. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]
- The transaction was structured as an acquisition of selected assets rather than of a
  whole going-concern company: the purchase agreement provided the rights to purchase
  certain rights, trademarks and copyrights to use the Advantage brand name, website and
  phone numbers. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]
- The agreement additionally provided an option to have assigned certain leases, fixed
  assets, airport concession agreements and other agreements associated with approximately
  20 locations that Advantage is or previously was operating. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]

## What crossed the boundary at the tier level, and what did not
- Customer-facing product / asset that crossed: the Advantage brand identity — brand name,
  website, phone numbers, trademarks and copyrights — i.e., the marketable brand rather
  than an intact operating company. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]
- Selected operational assets that could cross by option: leases, fixed assets and airport
  concession agreements tied to roughly 20 Advantage locations. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]
- The consideration for intangible assets acquired in 2009 was allocated primarily to the
  Advantage tradename and concession agreements (reported together with technology assets
  from a separate acquisition), and each transaction was accounted for using the
  acquisition method of accounting. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]
- People / management / organization: the primary describes the acquisition of brand
  assets and an option over selected location assets; it does not describe any transfer of
  Advantage's workforce, management, or an intact operating organization. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]
- Delivery through the acquirer's own organization: as of December 31, 2009 the registrant
  operated 24 corporate Advantage-brand rental locations in the United States — i.e., the
  brand was run through the acquirer's own corporate locations and operating processes.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]

## Transitional / shared-substrate arrangements at closing
- The FY2009 primary describes no transition-services agreement, operating agreement, or
  shared-services arrangement bridging Advantage's former operating substrate; the brand
  assets were folded directly into the registrant's existing car-rental operations. [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]

## Structural summary (closing only)
- The transaction transferred a customer-facing brand and its associated marks (name,
  website, phone numbers), plus an option over selected leases, fixed assets and airport
  concessions for about 20 locations, into an existing large car-rental operator; it did
  not transfer an intact producing/delivering organization, and the acquirer ran the brand
  through its own corporate locations, with no transitional bridging arrangement described.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-10-001717, Form 10-K (FY2009)]

[SLICE END]
